source.title: Semantic Structure of Feature Space in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and reports results on semantic feature geometry in LLMs, but it does not test the specific claims in the listed versions: it does not study sparse overcomplete toy networks, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAEs, or whether superposed features are one-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The reported semantic-axis geometry, low-dimensional structure, and steering spillovers are results on related feature geometry, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper's discussion of superposition and citations to other work are not themselves results. It does not test sparsity or feature importance.
record.test_reason: The study measures geometry (cosine similarity, PCA, steering spillover) of 32 contrastive semantic-axis directions in LLM residual streams and relates it to human ratings. It does not study sparse overcomplete toy networks, neuron polysemanticity, capacity allocation, SAE features, or whether features are 1-D vs multi-dimensional. Its superposition section is argument and citation, not a result on any version. Non-orthogonality of related, dense semantic features is a related but different construct from interference among sparse superposed features.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also argue that LLMs do not aim for near-orthogonality between important related features, but use geometric alignment to encode relations. They frame this as a counterpoint to the superposition view of almost-orthogonal storage, but give no test of superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study builds semantic axes from averaged activation differences for antonym pairs and measures their geometry and steering spillovers; it does not use or reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report smaller off-target spillovers in Llama 3.1 70B than in Llama 3.2 3B, and weaker on-target steering in the larger model. For Qwen3 1.7B, measured spillover appearance depends on probability versus logit change because baseline probabilities are often near 0 or 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarities among 32 LLM semantic axes track human scale correlations (r≈0.77–0.81). The top 3 PCs of raw axis vectors explain >45% (3B) and >33% (70B) of variance, versus 3.1% each if orthogonal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Related semantic feature directions in LLMs are substantially non-orthogonal and share a low-dimensional subspace mirroring human semantic associations.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along one semantic axis causes off-target spillovers that correlate with target/off-target cosine similarity (r 0.57–0.79 across four models). Spillovers are much smaller in 70B, alongside roughly 10x weaker on-target effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric alignment between LLM feature directions predicts cross-feature interference under steering.

record.problems: The reported axis-geometry and spillover correlations are presented in figures without uncertainty estimates. The study analyzes 32 constructed semantic axes and does not directly assess sparsity, capacity pressure, neuron-level feature distribution, or SAE feature quality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on the listed claim versions were reported. Figure 3 and Figure 7 show word-projection correlations with human ratings, but those address semantic-rating correspondence rather than the versions' claims about superposition or feature units.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or regular geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity/importance allocation.
No polysemantic neurons or alternative causes studied.
No measurement of feature spread across neurons and no SAE recovery; contrastive mean-difference directions only.
No SAE features assessed for completeness, stability or canonicity.
Axes are constructed as 1-D by design; dimensionality of superposed features not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to none. Two further results are unrecorded but bear on no version: the word-projection correlations in Figure 4 (top panels; r=0.881 and 0.868 for Llama, 0.688 and 0.772 for Qwen) and the CCA subspace alignment. No uncertainty is reported for any correlation, and the layers were chosen from preliminary exploration.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse overcomplete feature setting, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry as a function of sparsity is tested.
No capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions is tested.
No polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity are studied.
The study does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recover sparse features with an SAE.
The study does not assess SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
The study constructs and analyzes one-dimensional semantic-axis vectors, but does not test whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Llama 3.2 3B
rows.operation_detail: Added or subtracted a unit-normalized semantic-axis vector at the target-word token positions, with intervention magnitude α = 0.33 of the local residual-stream norm; measured spillover on off-target semantic scales.
rows.measure: Correlation between target/off-target axis cosine similarity and average spillover effect size
rows.note: The paper reports that more geometrically aligned axes predict larger, directionally consistent spillovers. It also says 70B spillovers are smaller than 3B.

rows.measure: Correlation between target/off-target axis cosine similarity and average spillover effect size
rows.note: The paper says spillover magnitude is much smaller in this model than in 3B, while on-target steering effects are also weaker.
